```{r}
#| label: setup-display
#| include: false

# Display-only render by default: reads saved CSV/PNG artifacts. No Seurat
# load, no loom export, no sbatch. Set TRUE intentionally to re-run the
# (cheap) aggregation / animal-level / permutation / figure scripts or to
# resubmit SLURM jobs.
run_analysis <- FALSE

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(knitr)
  library(glue)
  library(stringr)
  library(jsonlite)
  library(DT)
})

wkdir <- "/resnick/groups/mthomson/jboktor/WILDRxSPF_brains"
rscript <- "/resnick/groups/MazmanianLab/jboktor/software/miniforge3/envs/spatialomics/bin/Rscript"

report_fig_dir <- file.path(wkdir, "figures/SCENIC/report")
tbl_dir <- file.path(wkdir, "tables/SCENIC")
agg_proc_dir <- file.path(wkdir, "data/processed/scenic_by_class")
pilot_fig_dir <- file.path(wkdir, "figures/SCENIC/snRNASeq")

latest <- function(dir, pattern) {
  hits <- sort(list.files(dir, pattern = pattern, full.names = TRUE))
  if (length(hits)) tail(hits, 1) else NA_character_
}
read_latest <- function(pattern) {
  f <- latest(tbl_dir, pattern)
  if (is.na(f)) NULL else read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE)
}
not_computed <- function(what) {
  cat(glue("::: {{.callout-warning}}\n**{what} not yet computed** — set `run_analysis <- TRUE` and run the appendix cells.\n:::"), "\n\n")
}
# Embed a saved figure (path relative to notebooks/) or print a not-computed note
show_fig <- function(name, dir = report_fig_dir, rel = "../figures/SCENIC/report") {
  if (file.exists(file.path(dir, name))) cat(glue("![]({rel}/{name})"), "\n\n") else not_computed(name)
}
dt_table <- function(df, caption, page = 10, center = NULL) {
  datatable(df, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top", class = "compact stripe hover",
            extensions = "Buttons", caption = caption,
            options = list(pageLength = page, lengthMenu = unique(c(page, 25, 50, nrow(df))),
                           dom = "Bfrtip", buttons = list("colvis", "csv"), scrollX = TRUE,
                           columnDefs = if (length(center)) list(list(className = "dt-center", targets = center)) else list()))
}
rel <- function(p) sub(paste0(wkdir, "/"), "", p, fixed = TRUE)
big <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")

# Class-level artifacts (date-only file names; the _subclass/_supertype files carry a suffix)
d8 <- "\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}\\.csv$"
tests_csv <- latest(tbl_dir, paste0("^SCENIC_animal_level_tests_", d8))
split_disp_csv <- latest(tbl_dir, paste0("^SCENIC_split_summary_display_", d8))
tests <- if (!is.na(tests_csv)) read_csv(tests_csv, show_col_types = FALSE) else NULL
agg <- if (file.exists(file.path(agg_proc_dir, "aggregate_summary.json")))
  fromJSON(file.path(agg_proc_dir, "aggregate_summary.json")) else NULL

# Multi-level artifacts
lvl <- read_latest(paste0("^SCENIC_level_summary_display_", d8))
perm_split <- read_latest(paste0("^SCENIC_split_permutation_tests_", d8))
circuit <- read_latest(paste0("^SCENIC_popalign_circuit_permutation_display_", d8))
hits_all <- read_latest(paste0("^SCENIC_fdr_hits_all_levels_display_", d8))
n_fit <- sapply(c(class = "", subclass = "_subclass", supertype = "_supertype"), function(s) {
  f <- latest(tbl_dir, paste0("^SCENIC_animal_level_split_summary", s, "_", d8))
  if (is.na(f)) NA_integer_ else nrow(read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE))
})

# Headline numbers (NA if artifacts are missing)
n_cell_hits <- if (!is.null(agg)) agg$n_sig_tests else NA
if (!is.null(lvl)) {
  by_lv <- lvl %>% group_by(Level) %>%
    summarise(grns = sum(GRNs), tests = sum(Tests), nom = sum(`p < 0.05`), exp = sum(`Expected (5%)`),
              fdr = sum(`FDR < 0.10 (split)`), glob = sum(`FDR < 0.10 (global)`),
              sep = sum(`Complete separation (6 vs 6)`), sep_exp = sum(`Expected separations`),
              perm_min = min(`Permutation p (excess)`), .groups = "drop")
  lv <- function(l, col) by_lv[[col]][by_lv$Level == l]
  tot_tests <- sum(by_lv$tests); tot_nom <- sum(by_lv$nom); tot_exp <- sum(by_lv$exp)
  tot_fdr <- sum(by_lv$fdr); tot_glob <- sum(by_lv$glob)
  tot_sep <- sum(by_lv$sep); tot_sep_exp <- sum(by_lv$sep_exp)
  perm_min <- min(lvl$`Permutation p (excess)`)
}
if (!is.null(perm_split)) {
  ps_n <- nrow(perm_split); ps_nom <- sum(perm_split$p_perm < 0.05)
  ps_fdr <- sum(perm_split$fdr_perm_level < 0.10)
}
if (!is.null(circuit)) {
  ci_n <- nrow(circuit); ci_nom <- sum(circuit$`Permutation p` < 0.05)
  ci_obs <- sum(circuit$`p < 0.05 observed`); ci_exp <- round(sum(circuit$`Permutation mean`))
}
if (!is.null(tests)) {
  ch <- tests %>% filter(cell_level_hit)
  n_ch_nom <- sum(ch$p_animal < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
  pct_ch_sign <- round(100 * mean(sign(ch$delta_cell) == sign(ch$delta_animal), na.rm = TRUE))
  med_g_ch <- round(median(abs(ch$hedges_g), na.rm = TRUE), 2)
  med_rel_ch <- round(100 * median(abs(ch$delta_cell) / ((ch$animal_mean_SPF + ch$animal_mean_WildR) / 2), na.rm = TRUE), 1)
  pct_ch_p25 <- round(100 * mean(ch$p_animal < 0.25, na.rm = TRUE))
  pct_all_p25 <- round(100 * mean(tests$p_animal < 0.25, na.rm = TRUE))
}
if (!is.null(hits_all)) {
  n_hits_low <- sum(pmax(hits_all$`Mean AUC SPF`, hits_all$`Mean AUC WildR`) < 0.005)
  med_hit_nuclei <- round(median(hits_all$Nuclei))
}
mde_g <- round(power.t.test(n = 6, power = 0.8, sig.level = 0.05)$delta, 1)
n_needed <- ceiling(power.t.test(delta = 0.6, power = 0.8, sig.level = 0.05)$n)
```

# Microbiome Effects on Transcription-Factor Regulon Activity (pySCENIC)

## Overview

We asked whether WildR and SPF mice differ in **transcription-factor regulon activity** in the amygdala (AMY) and hypothalamus (HYP). pySCENIC was fitted separately for every tissue × Allen cell type at three resolutions: **`r n_fit[["class"]]` class, `r n_fit[["subclass"]]` subclass and `r n_fit[["supertype"]]` supertype GRNs** (`r sum(n_fit)` in total). Every regulon was then tested on per-animal mean AUCell, 6 WildR vs 6 SPF animals per tissue, because the animal is the unit of replication. **The answer is no, at every resolution.**

- Of `r big(tot_tests)` regulon tests, `r big(tot_nom)` reach nominal p < 0.05. Chance alone predicts ≈`r big(tot_exp)`.
- **No test survives correction across GRNs** at any level.
- Relabelling the 12 animals 924 ways gives the exact null for this design. The observed result sits in the middle or lower part of that null in every level × tissue (permutation p ≥ `r perm_min`).

The `r n_cell_hits` "significant regulons" from the original per-nucleus tests were pseudoreplication. Their direction is mostly real, but they are about a third of the size that 6 vs 6 animals can detect. **Use this analysis as a regulon catalogue and a source of weak hypotheses, not as evidence for microbiome-driven TF programs.**

```{r}
#| label: display-stats
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (is.null(lvl)) {
  not_computed("Multi-level animal-level summary")
} else {
  stat <- function(v, l) cat(glue("::: {{.stat}}\n[{v}]{{.stat-value}}\n[{l}]{{.stat-label}}\n:::"), "\n\n")
  cat("::: {.stat-row}\n\n")
  stat(sum(n_fit), "GRNs fitted (class + subclass + supertype)")
  stat(big(tot_tests), "Regulon tests at the animal level")
  stat(glue("{big(tot_nom)} vs {big(tot_exp)}"), "p < 0.05 observed vs expected by chance")
  stat(tot_glob, "Tests passing FDR < 0.10 across GRNs")
  cat(":::\n\n")
}
```

## Background

Microbiome status shifts gene expression and cell state in specific amygdalar and hypothalamic populations in this cohort. These are concentrated in the MeA–BST–medial-hypothalamus network (see the MAST DEG, D-SPIN and popAlign notebooks). SCENIC asks the upstream question: which **regulons** change activity? A regulon is a TF plus the co-expressed target genes that carry its binding motif. A regulon that shifts consistently between groups would be a candidate mechanistic driver to follow up spatially and experimentally.

Three design facts govern how the results can be read:

1. **A GRN is fitted separately for each split.** Regulons are therefore only comparable within a split, and comparisons across splits must use standardized effects (Hedges g, within-split z). Splitting finer gives cell-type-specific networks but fewer nuclei per GRN.
2. **There are 6 animals per microbiome group in each tissue.** All three resolutions reuse the same 12 animals per tissue, so agreement across levels is not independent replication. At 6 vs 6, 80% power at α = 0.05 requires Hedges g ≈ `r mde_g`.
3. **Thousands of regulons are tested.** With hundreds of GRNs, a handful of within-GRN FDR hits and complete-separation patterns are expected by chance alone. This report compares every count against its null.

## Results

### 537 GRNs at three resolutions, most with all 12 animals

::: {.figure-card .fig-wide}
```{r}
#| label: display-levels-coverage
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fig("SCENIC_levels_coverage.png")
```

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 1.**]{.fig-num} Design and coverage of the testable GRNs at each Allen resolution (class: 35 of 36 testable). (A) Nuclei per GRN (log scale). (B) Share of GRNs by how many animals per group contribute ≥ 10 nuclei. An animal enters the test only above that floor, and a GRN needs ≥ 3 animals per group. (C) Regulons retained per GRN after cisTarget motif pruning.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- All GRNs ran `grn → ctx → aucell` on raw UMI counts and passed the animal-level test stage: `r n_fit[["class"]]` class, `r n_fit[["subclass"]]` subclass and `r n_fit[["supertype"]]` supertype. HYP `21 MB Dopa` is the only class-level GRN that is untestable (4 vs 2 animals).
- Finer splits are smaller. The median GRN shrinks from ~2–3k nuclei (class) to ~500 (supertype), yet 63–83% of GRNs at every level still have all **6 vs 6 animals**. A null result therefore reflects effect size and replication, not missing animals.
- Smaller GRNs call *more* regulons: the median rises from 156–182 at class level to 208–215 at supertype. Large heterogeneous neuronal classes retain the fewest. Hit counts must be compared as rates against a null, never as raw totals.
:::

[Source: cell `cell-fig-report`](#cell-fig-report){.provenance}
:::

### The original cell-level hits were pseudoreplication

::: {.figure-card .fig-wide}
```{r}
#| label: display-cell-vs-animal
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fig("SCENIC_cell_vs_animal_level.png")
```

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 2.**]{.fig-num} Why the original class-level hit counts cannot be read as microbiome effects. (A) Regulons significant in the per-class, nucleus-level Wilcoxon test (BH padj < 0.05) against nuclei in the class. (B) The same `r n_cell_hits` cell-level hits re-tested on per-animal mean AUCell (pooled-variance t-test, 6 vs 6); the dashed line is the count expected per bin if none were real. (C) The single most significant cell-level hit, one point per animal (size = nuclei); bars are group means.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- Cell-level hit counts track **how many nuclei a class has**. HY GABA/Glut and OPC-Oligo, with 37–49k nuclei each, report dozens of hits from ΔAUC ≈ 0.001.
- Only **`r n_ch_nom` of `r n_cell_hits`** cell-level hits reach nominal p < 0.05 on animal means, close to the 5% expected by chance. The extreme case, Bclaf1(+) in HYP HY Glut, goes from p = 8 × 10⁻¹⁰⁵ to p = 0.54. Its six WildR animals span the entire SPF range.
- The hits are not pure noise. `r pct_ch_sign`% keep their sign per animal, and `r pct_ch_p25`% have animal-level p < 0.25 (vs `r pct_all_p25`% of all regulons). They are **small, directionally coherent shifts** (median `r med_rel_ch`% change in AUC, |g| ≈ `r med_g_ch`) that 6 vs 6 animals cannot confirm. Detecting g ≈ 0.6 at 80% power would need ~`r n_needed` animals per group.
- The old hit tables ([data/processed/scenic_by_class/top_hits_padj05.csv]{.path}, `tf_hit_recurrence.csv`) and their recurrent TFs (Rfx3, Bclaf1, Klf12, Bptf) should not be cited as microbiome-regulated regulons.
:::

[Source: cell `cell-tbl-animal-level`](#cell-tbl-animal-level){.provenance}
:::

### No resolution shows more signal than chance

::: {.figure-card .fig-wide}
```{r}
#| label: display-levels-null
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fig("SCENIC_levels_null.png")
```

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 3.**]{.fig-num} Global tests for any microbiome effect on regulon activity at each resolution. (A) QQ plot of all animal-level p-values against the uniform null. (B) Tests at nominal p < 0.05 against 5% of tests. (C) Exact permutation null for each level × tissue. The tissue's 12 animals were relabelled in all 924 ways, the same relabelling was applied to every GRN at once (which keeps the correlation between regulons and between GRNs), and tests at p < 0.05 were counted. The orange line marks the observed count. (D) Per-GRN permutation p for an excess of p < 0.05 tests (all relabellings of that GRN's animals); the dashed line is the uniform expectation.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- **Every level is null.** Nominal p < 0.05 occurs *less* often than 5% at every resolution: class `r lv("class","nom")` vs `r lv("class","exp")`, subclass `r big(lv("subclass","nom"))` vs `r big(lv("subclass","exp"))`, supertype `r big(lv("supertype","nom"))` vs `r big(lv("supertype","exp"))`. The QQ curves lie on or below the diagonal.
- The permutation null (C) is the right yardstick, because regulons are correlated and the 5% line understates how widely the count can vary under no effect. It has a long right tail: some relabellings of the 12 animals produce far more hits than the true WildR/SPF labels. Animals do differ systematically, but **not along the microbiome axis**. The observed count sits at or below the null median in all six level × tissue panels (permutation p ≥ `r perm_min`).
- Per GRN (D), `r ps_nom` of `r ps_n` GRNs reach permutation p < 0.05 (≈`r round(0.05*ps_n)` expected), and none survives FDR within its level (`r ps_fdr`). A naïve binomial test would have flagged 3 supertypes; under permutation they are ordinary.
- Complete 6 vs 6 separation of animals, the most striking pattern in a superplot, occurs `r tot_sep` times against ≈`r tot_sep_exp` expected by chance (2/924 per test).
:::

[Source: cell `cell-tbl-permutation`](#cell-tbl-permutation) · [cell `cell-fig-report`](#cell-fig-report){.provenance}
:::

### The few within-GRN hits are isolated, low-activity and do not replicate

::: {.figure-card .fig-wide}
```{r}
#| label: display-hit-superplots
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fig("SCENIC_fdr_hits_superplots.png")
```

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 4.**]{.fig-num} The 12 strongest within-GRN FDR < 0.10 regulons across all levels (GRNs with ≥ 5 animals per group). One point per animal, sized by nuclei; bars are group means. Panel titles give the regulon, tissue, level, split, within-GRN q and Hedges g. None passes FDR after correcting across GRNs.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- `r tot_fdr` regulons pass FDR < 0.10 *within* their own GRN: `r lv("class","fdr")` at class, `r lv("subclass","fdr")` at subclass and `r lv("supertype","fdr")` at supertype level. That is about what testing `r sum(n_fit)` GRNs separately would yield by chance, and **zero survive correction across GRNs**.
- They look like multiplicity, not biology:
  - **Each of the `r tot_fdr` is a different GRN × TF pair**, and none recurs at a second level in the same tissue and direction.
  - **Many are near-zero-activity regulons.** `r n_hits_low` of `r tot_fdr` have mean AUC < 0.005; Lef1(+) in AMY IT EP-CLA sits at 0.00004 vs 0.00025. In that range a few target genes moving can drive the score.
  - **Most come from small GRNs** (median `r med_hit_nuclei` nuclei).
- The class-level MB GABA leads (Irf2, Crebl2, Usf2; SPF-higher) do **not** reappear in the MB GABA subclass or supertypes. The panels look clean because a single 6 vs 6 split with g ≈ 3 is what a few hundred GRN × regulon tests produce by chance.
:::

[Source: cell `cell-tbl-animal-level-subclass`](#cell-tbl-animal-level-subclass) · [cell `cell-fig-report`](#cell-fig-report){.provenance}
:::

### The circuits flagged by popAlign carry no extra regulon signal

A prespecified, better-powered question: do the populations where popAlign found microbiome-associated **cell-state or abundance shifts** show more regulon signal than the rest? These include MEA-BST Lhx6 Nr2e1 / Lhx6 Sp9 / Otp Zic2, DMH Hmx2, TMd-DMH Foxd2, PVHd-DMH Lhx6 and PVH-SO-PVa Otp. The test below uses every subclass and supertype GRN in those populations.

```{r}
#| label: display-circuit-table
#| echo: false
if (!is.null(circuit)) {
  dt_table(circuit, page = 10, center = 3:7,
           caption = "Subclass/supertype GRNs in the popAlign-flagged MeA–BST–medial-hypothalamus populations, sorted by per-GRN permutation p for an excess of p < 0.05 regulon tests.")
} else not_computed("popAlign-circuit permutation table")
```

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- Across the `r ci_n` circuit GRNs, `r ci_obs` regulon tests reach p < 0.05 against `r ci_exp` expected under permutation. `r ci_nom` GRNs reach permutation p < 0.05, against ≈`r round(0.05*ci_n, 1)` expected by chance.
- The exact supertypes where popAlign's state shifts were strongest are unremarkable here: MEA-BST Lhx6 Nr2e1 Gaba_2 (`0355`) and DMH Hmx2 Gaba_2 (`0488`).
- The three nominal circuit GRNs (AMY MEA-BST Lhx6 Sp9 Gaba_3, HYP PVH-SO-PVa Otp Glut_6, HYP DMH Hmx2 Gaba_3) are sibling supertypes of popAlign leads. They are worth noting but are not more than chance.
- Interpretation: the popAlign state shifts are **not accompanied by detectable whole-regulon reprogramming**. They are more likely to involve changes in target-gene sets that pySCENIC does not group into one regulon, or TFs that cisTarget did not call.
:::

Permutation tables: [`r rel(latest(tbl_dir, paste0("^SCENIC_split_permutation_tests_", d8)))`]{.path} · [`r rel(latest(tbl_dir, paste0("^SCENIC_level_permutation_tests_", d8)))`]{.path}

### No TF program is consistent across cell types or resolutions

::: {.figure-card .fig-wide}
```{r}
#| label: display-consensus
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fig("SCENIC_tf_consensus_levels.png")
```

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 5.**]{.fig-num} Cross-GRN TF consensus at each level. This asks whether a TF moves the same way across *all* cell types of a tissue, which is the best-powered test for a broad microbiome effect. For each TF whose activating regulon was called in ≥ 3 GRNs of a tissue, the 12 animal means were z-scored within each GRN, each animal's z was averaged across GRNs, and 6 vs 6 was tested once per TF × tissue (BH within tissue). (A) Consensus Hedges g against −log10 p, by tissue (rows) and level (columns); orange = candidate TFs from earlier analyses; the four strongest per panel are labelled. (B) Consensus g of the candidate TFs at each level; point size = GRNs pooled.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- **No TF passes FDR < 0.10 in the consensus test at any level.** The strongest tests (AMY Zfp324/Esr1/Glis1; HYP Banp/Zfp207/Zbtb34) differ at each level, and consensus effects agree only weakly between levels (r ≈ 0.25).
- The cell-level "recurrent" TFs **Rfx3, Bptf and Bclaf1 change sign** between tissues or levels. Their recurrence reflected that broadly active regulons get tested in nearly every GRN.
- **HYP Mllt10, Zbtb20 and Klf12** are the only candidates whose sign holds at all three levels (WildR-higher; g ≈ 0.5–1.0, p ≥ 0.1 throughout). Ube2k is WildR-higher in HYP at class level but weakens at finer levels. Because every level reuses the same 12 animals, this consistency is a weak hypothesis, not replication.
:::

[Source: cell `cell-tbl-animal-level`](#cell-tbl-animal-level) · [cell `cell-fig-report`](#cell-fig-report){.provenance}
:::

::: {.figure-card .fig-wide}
```{r}

#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fig("SCENIC_recurrent_tf_effects.png")
```

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 6.**]{.fig-num} Class level: the 24 TFs most often reported as cell-level hits, across every class GRN in which their activating regulon was called. Tile colour = animal-level Hedges g (WildR − SPF, clipped at ±2.5); blank = not called in that class. ○ = cell-level hit (padj < 0.05); ✱ = animal-level p < 0.05.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- Almost no cell-level circle carries an animal-level star, and the recurrent TFs flip colour between classes.
- Mllt10(+) and Ube2k(+) are mostly orange (WildR-higher) across HYP classes, which is the origin of the candidate above.
- Glial identity regulons (Spi1, Irf8, Ikzf1, Fli1 in OPC-Oligo / Astro-Epen) flip sign between AMY and HYP. That more likely reflects different microglial contamination of those classes than a microbiome response.
:::

(A) Regulon Specificity Score (Jensen–Shannon based) for the top five regulons in each of the 12 largest subclasses. (B) UMAP of AUCell regulon space coloured by subclass and microbiome, with the four most variable regulons.

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- The pipeline recovers textbook identity TFs: Myb / Irx5 (ependymal), Runx1 / Irf5 / Irf8 / Ikzf1 (microglia) and Sox10 (oligodendrocytes). This confirms that gene-symbol cleaning, the cisTarget databases and AUCell work on this Parse data. The null microbiome result is not a broken pipeline.
- Neuronal subclasses have weak specificity in a single pooled GRN (RSS < 0.1). That is why production fitted one GRN per class, subclass and supertype.
- In regulon space, the microbiome groups mix within subclasses. Cell identity is the dominant axis.
:::

[Source: cell `cell-fig-report`](#cell-fig-report) (A) · [cell `cell-run-pipeline`](#cell-run-pipeline) (B){.provenance}
:::

### Conclusions

- **pySCENIC detects no microbiome effect on regulon activity at animal resolution, at any Allen level.**
  - Across `r sum(n_fit)` GRNs and `r big(tot_tests)` regulon tests, the p-value distribution, the exact permutation null and the complete-separation counts all match no effect.
  - The `r tot_fdr` within-GRN FDR hits do not survive correction across GRNs and do not recur across levels.
- **The earlier "`r n_cell_hits` significant regulons" were pseudoreplication.**
  - Nucleus-level tests turned ~`r med_rel_ch`% AUC shifts into p-values as small as 10⁻¹⁰⁵.
  - The shifts are mostly in the right direction. But their typical size (g ≈ `r med_g_ch`) is about a third of what 6 vs 6 animals can detect (g ≈ `r mde_g`).
- **Even the circuits with independent microbiome evidence show no regulon signal.** The MeA–BST–medial-hypothalamus populations where popAlign found state shifts look like the rest. Whatever moves cell state there is not a whole-regulon TF program that AUCell can see.
- **What survives as hypothesis only:**
  - WildR-higher Mllt10(+), Zbtb20(+) and Klf12(+) across HYP cell types: same sign at three levels, never significant, same animals throughout.
  - SPF-higher Irf2 / Crebl2 / Usf2 in HYP MB GABA and WildR-higher Npas2 / Gli2 in HYP microglia. These are class-level only and did not replicate at finer resolution.

## Next Steps

- **Stop investing compute in pySCENIC for this contrast.** Three resolutions of GRNs give the same null, and finer splits only add tests. Power is the binding constraint: detecting the observed shift size (g ≈ `r med_g_ch`) at 80% power needs ~`r n_needed` animals per group.
- **Use the regulons as features, not endpoints.** The regulon catalogue (per-GRN `regulons.csv`, AUCell matrices) is still useful to *annotate* effects found elsewhere. For example, check which regulons contain the popAlign state-shift genes (*Erbb4*, *Htr2c*, *Reln*, *Zbtb20*) and the MAST DEGs in the same populations. That is target-level enrichment, a different question from regulon-activity change.
- **If one hypothesis is pursued, make it HYP Mllt10 / Zbtb20 / Klf12**, the only signals with a consistent sign. Check per-animal depth first (`mean_auc ~ group + log10 median UMI`), then validate a few targets in seqFISH, where more animals or sections can be added.
- **Retire the old outputs from citation.** `data/processed/scenic_by_class/top_hits_padj05.csv`, `tf_hit_recurrence.csv` and the `_aggregate/` figures are superseded by the animal-level tables in [tables/SCENIC/]{.path}.
- **Optional:** the class GRNs were not refitted after the switch to the animal-level test (their AUCell matrices are unchanged), so no refit is needed. If one is ever wanted for a new loom set, write it to a new `by_class_<date>` folder, not over `by_class/`.

# Code & Provenance {.code-appendix}

All heavy steps are recorded below but gated by `run_analysis` (default `FALSE`), so rendering never re-exports looms, refits GRNs or submits jobs. The post-hoc scripts (aggregate, animal-level tests, permutation, figures) read saved outputs only and run in under a minute on a login node.

## Inputs and run design

pySCENIC runs **one GRN per tissue × Allen split** with both microbiome groups in each loom, at class, subclass and supertype resolution. Input is the Seurat `RNA` **`counts`** layer (raw UMIs) from `seurat_obj_onlyparsefilters_celltyped_2025-12-27.rds` (`keep_cell`). Export checked that nonzeros are 100% integer and non-negative (median library size ~13.5k) and refuses to write a loom otherwise. `Symbol-GRCm39` names are stripped to bare symbols for the cisTarget TF overlap.

- **Class (36 GRNs).** AMY `01 IT-ET Glut` (87k nuclei) timed out at 3 days. It was stratified-subsampled to 45k nuclei (microbiome × subclass) and finished in ~3 h with 450G; the full loom is kept as `*_full87k.*`.
- **Subclass (137) and supertype (364) GRNs.** Looms were sliced from the class looms (raw UMIs; full 87k AMY IT-ET loom), and genes were re-filtered to those detected in ≥ 10 nuclei. A split is eligible with ≥ 100 nuclei, ≥ 30 per group and ≥ 3 animals per group with ≥ 10 nuclei. Of 310 tissue × subclass combinations, 137 qualified; 364 supertypes qualified.
- **Whole-tissue GRNs (AMY / HYP, ~190–200k nuclei) were discontinued.** Both jobs ran to the 7-day walltime without finishing `pyscenic grn`, at only ~90–95G of 600G, which points to a dask/Numba worker-fork stall.
- **Contrast.** Since 2026-10-06, `run_scenic_one_split.R` runs the animal-level test via [notebooks/R_scripts/scenic_animal_level_helpers.R]{.path}:
  - per-animal mean AUCell, animals with ≥ 10 nuclei, ≥ 3 animals per group;
  - pooled-variance t-test (≡ `lm(mean ~ group)`), plus Hedges g, Cliff's δ, exact Wilcoxon and complete-separation counts;
  - BH within split.

  The original nucleus-level Wilcoxon (`diff_regulons_WildR_vs_SPF.csv`, `run_summary_celllevel.json`) is kept for the record.

| Role | Path |
|------|------|
| cisTarget DBs / TF list | [data/input/scenic/cisTarget/]{.path} |
| Class looms, metadata, manifest | [data/input/scenic/snRNASeq/]{.path} |
| Subclass / supertype looms, metadata, manifests, array lists | [data/interim/scenic/looms_{subclass,supertype}/]{.path} |
| Per-GRN outputs (`adjacencies`, `regulons`, `auc_mtx`, animal-level diff, `run_summary.json`) | [data/interim/scenic/by_{class,subclass,supertype}/&lt;stem&gt;/]{.path} |
| Per-animal means, TF consensus scores, permutation null | [data/interim/scenic/animal_level/]{.path} |
| Result + display tables | [tables/SCENIC/]{.path} |
| Report figures | [figures/SCENIC/report/]{.path} |
| Nucleus-level aggregation (superseded) | [data/processed/scenic_by_class/]{.path}, [figures/SCENIC/snRNASeq_by_class/_aggregate/]{.path} |
| Pilot (5k subsample) | [data/processed/scenic/]{.path}, [figures/SCENIC/snRNASeq/]{.path} |
| SLURM logs / job lists | [.cluster_runs/scenic/]{.path} |

## Class GRNs: export looms and submit (SLURM)

`run_scenic_export_and_submit.sh` exports the class looms and submits one `sbatch` job per class (default 24 CPU / 300G / 3 d).

```{r}
#| label: cell-scenic-launch
#| eval: !expr run_analysis

source(file.path(wkdir, "notebooks/R_scripts/_misc_functions.R"))
cmd <- glue("sbatch {wkdir}/notebooks/shell_scripts/run_scenic_export_and_submit.sh")
print(cmd)
shell_do(cmd)
```

```{r}
#| label: cell-scenic-check
#| eval: !expr run_analysis

for (lv in c("class", "subclass", "supertype")) {
  done <- list.files(file.path(wkdir, "data/interim/scenic", paste0("by_", lv)),
                     pattern = "run_summary\\.json$", recursive = TRUE)
  message(lv, ": ", length(done), " run summaries")
}
```

## Subclass- and supertype-level GRNs (SLURM, 2026-10-06)

[notebooks/python_scripts/export_scenic_subclass_looms.py]{.path} slices the class looms; [notebooks/shell_scripts/run_pyscenic_subclass_array.sh]{.path} runs `run_scenic_one_split.R` on line *i* of a loom list. Two resource tiers were sized from the class runs (49k nuclei used 85 GB / 2.4 h at 24 CPUs):

| Step | Job | Tasks | Resources | State |
|------|-----|-------|-----------|-------|
| Subclass loom export | 4096829 | 1 | 4 CPU / 64G (37 min, 11.8 GB peak) | completed |
| Subclass GRNs, < 5k nuclei | 4099811 | 120 | 16 CPU / 64G / 12 h, ≤ 20 concurrent | 100 completed, 20 failed at test stage → rerun |
| Subclass GRNs, ≥ 5k nuclei | 4099812 | 17 | 24 CPU / 160G / 1 d, ≤ 8 concurrent | 9 completed, 8 failed at test stage → rerun |
| Supertype loom export | 4100108 | 1 | 4 CPU / 64G (1 h 28 min) | completed |
| Supertype GRNs, < 5k nuclei | 4106625 | 352 | as subclass small tier | 352 completed |
| Supertype GRNs, ≥ 5k nuclei | 4106626 | 12 | as subclass large tier | 12 completed |

Logs: `.cluster_runs/scenic/log_pyscenic_subclass_<jobid>_<task>.{log,err}` (dask "stream closed" tracebacks at shutdown are benign); job lists `.cluster_runs/scenic/submitted_jobs_{subclass,supertype}_2026-10-06.txt`. The largest splits were AMY 009 L2/3 IT PIR-ENTl Glut (34k nuclei, subclass) and HYP 1184 MOL NN_4 (28k, supertype), so no subsampling was needed.

::: {.callout-note}
**Run incident (2026-10-06).** 28 subclass tasks (small 0–19, large 0–7) failed with an R parse error. `run_scenic_one_split.R` was edited while they ran, and `Rscript` reads its file incrementally. All 28 had already finished `grn → ctx → aucell`, so only the animal-level test stage was rerun on the saved outputs (log `.cluster_runs/scenic/log_subclass_rerun_teststage_*.log`), with no GRN refit. The array worker now runs a private snapshot of the runner taken at task start. All 137 subclass and 364 supertype `run_summary.json` files carry the animal-level test.
:::

```{r}
#| label: cell-scenic-subclass-export
#| eval: !expr run_analysis

shell_do(glue("sbatch {wkdir}/notebooks/shell_scripts/run_scenic_export_subclass.sh"))
shell_do(glue("sbatch --export=ALL,LEVEL=supertype {wkdir}/notebooks/shell_scripts/run_scenic_export_subclass.sh"))
```

```{r}
#| label: cell-scenic-subclass-submit
#| eval: !expr run_analysis

S <- file.path(wkdir, "notebooks/shell_scripts/run_pyscenic_subclass_array.sh")
for (lv in c("subclass", "supertype")) {
  L <- file.path(wkdir, glue("data/interim/scenic/looms_{lv}"))
  n_small <- length(Filter(nzchar, readLines(file.path(L, glue("looms_{lv}_small.txt")))))
  n_large <- length(Filter(nzchar, readLines(file.path(L, glue("looms_{lv}_large.txt")))))
  shell_do(glue("sbatch --array=0-{n_small - 1}%20 {S} -l {L}/looms_{lv}_small.txt"))
  shell_do(glue("sbatch --array=0-{n_large - 1}%8 --cpus-per-task=24 --mem=160G --time=1-00:00:00 {S} -l {L}/looms_{lv}_large.txt"))
}
```

## Animal-level regulon tests

[notebooks/R_scripts/test_scenic_regulons_animal_level.R]{.path} recomputes the per-split animal-level test from the saved AUCell matrices with the shared helper. It adds BH-FDR within split (primary) and across all tests of a level (global). The cross-split TF consensus z-scores animal means within each split, averages them per animal across the splits where the TF's (+) regulon was called (≥ 3), and runs one 6 vs 6 test per TF × tissue. At class level it also joins the original nucleus-level result. Run directly on 2026-10-06 (seconds per level).

```{r}
#| label: cell-tbl-animal-level
#| eval: !expr run_analysis

# Writes (date-stamped):
#   tables/SCENIC/SCENIC_animal_level_tests_<date>.csv
#   tables/SCENIC/SCENIC_animal_level_split_summary_<date>.csv
#   tables/SCENIC/SCENIC_tf_consensus_animal_level_<date>.csv
#   data/interim/scenic/animal_level/regulon_auc_per_animal_<date>.csv
#   data/interim/scenic/animal_level/regulon_tf_consensus_per_animal_<date>.csv
system2(rscript, c(file.path(wkdir, "notebooks/R_scripts/test_scenic_regulons_animal_level.R"),
                   "--level", "class"))
```

```{r}
#| label: cell-tbl-animal-level-subclass
#| eval: !expr run_analysis

# Same outputs with a _subclass / _supertype suffix
for (lv in c("subclass", "supertype")) {
  system2(rscript, c(file.path(wkdir, "notebooks/R_scripts/test_scenic_regulons_animal_level.R"),
                     "--level", lv))
}
```

## Permutation tests (2026-10-07)

[notebooks/R_scripts/test_scenic_split_permutation.R]{.path} tests for an excess of p < 0.05 regulon tests by relabelling the microbiome group over animals, which keeps the correlation between regulons.

- **Per GRN:** every relabelling of that GRN's eligible animals is enumerated (≤ 924).
- **Per level × tissue:** one relabelling of the tissue's 12 animals is applied to all GRNs jointly, because the animals are shared across GRNs.
  - A GRN whose relabelled groups fall below 3 animals contributes its null expectation (0.05 × regulons).
  - The observed totals reproduce the counts in the test tables (143 / 850 / 2,812).

Run directly on 2026-10-07 in 41 s; log `.cluster_runs/scenic/log_split_permutation_2026-10-07_1118.log`.

```{r}
#| label: cell-tbl-permutation
#| eval: !expr run_analysis

# Writes tables/SCENIC/SCENIC_{split,level}_permutation_tests_<date>.csv and
# data/interim/scenic/animal_level/level_permutation_null_<date>.csv
system2(rscript, c(file.path(wkdir, "notebooks/R_scripts/test_scenic_split_permutation.R"), "2026-10-06"))
```
